title: Etale scheme charts compute the same local dimension of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with point set $|X|$ [def-a1-space-point-topology]. An etale scheme chart means a representable etale morphism $a:W\to X$ from an $S$-scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For each $x\in|X|$ there exist such a chart and a point $w\in W$ with $a(w)=x$. If $a_i:W_i\to X$ are two such charts and $w_i\in W_i$ satisfy $a_i(w_i)=x$, then $$\dim\mathcal O_{W_1,w_1}=\dim\mathcal O_{W_2,w_2}.$$ Here $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is the stalk of the scheme structure sheaf, and ring dimension is [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Thus these dimensions define a unique value $\delta_X(x)\in\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$. When $X$ is represented by a scheme $T$, and $t\in T$ corresponds to $x$, this value equals $\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}$. No quasi-separatedness, Noetherian, or finite-dimensionality hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BAM (lemma-pre-dimension-local-ring), including its last sentence for schemes; Tag 04NA (definition-dimension-local-ring).

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a:W\to X$ from the definition of algebraic space. Its point map is surjective by the point-surjectivity criterion, so every $x\in|X|$ has a lift $w\in W$. This proves the existence clause without any quasi-compactness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BAM (lemma-pre-dimension-local-ring), expanding Tag 04N2 through the common chart; Tag 04NA (definition-dimension-local-ring).

proof.text: For the given two charts form the sheaf fibre product $R=W_1\times_XW_2$. It is a scheme because $a_2$ is representable and $W_1$ is a scheme. The projection $p_1:R\to W_1$ is etale by the definition of representable etaleness; interchange the indices for $p_2$. Since $w_1,w_2$ have the same image $x$ in $|X|$, the fibre-product point lemma gives a scheme point $r\in R$ with $p_i(r)=w_i$. Neither chart is required to be surjective.

source.place: Tag 0BAM (lemma-pre-dimension-local-ring), expanding Tag 04N2 through the common chart; Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian) for the common point; Tag 04NA (definition-dimension-local-ring).

proof.text: For each $i$ choose affine opens $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i\subset W_i$ and $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i\subset R$, containing $w_i$ and $r$, with $p_i(U_i)\subset V_i$ and $A_i\to B_i$ etale. Such pairs cover an etale morphism by its affine-local definition. Write $\mathfrak q_i$ for the prime of $r$ in $B_i$ and $\mathfrak p_i$ for that of $w_i$ in $A_i$; the scheme morphism gives $\mathfrak p_i=(A_i\to B_i)^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$. Affine stalk localization identifies $\mathcal O_{W_i,w_i}\cong(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and $\mathcal O_{R,r}\cong(B_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$. Apply the etale ring-dimension lemma to obtain $\dim\mathcal O_{W_i,w_i}=\dim\mathcal O_{R,r}$. Ring isomorphisms preserve dimension because inverse image bijects prime chains, preserving strict inclusions.

source.place: Tag 04N8 (lemma-dimension-local-ring-local), using more-algebra.tex Tag 07QP (lemma-dimension-etale-extension) and schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves).

proof.text: The two equalities from step 3 give $\dim\mathcal O_{W_1,w_1}=\dim\mathcal O_{R,r}=\dim\mathcal O_{W_2,w_2}$. Choose one lifted chart from step 1 and define $\delta_X(x)$ to be its stalk dimension. This is nonnegative or infinite: a stalk at a scheme point is a nonzero local ring and its maximal ideal is prime, giving a chain of length zero. Step 3 shows independence of the choice; any value satisfying the chart equalities must equal this chosen one. This proves existence and uniqueness of the value, including infinite dimension.

source.place: Tag 0BAM (lemma-pre-dimension-local-ring), expanding Tag 04N2 through the common chart; Tag 04NA (definition-dimension-local-ring).

proof.text: If $X$ is represented by a scheme $T$, the identity $T\to T$ is an etale chart, and the point corresponding to $x$ is $t$. Comparing any chart to this identity chart by steps 2--4 gives $\delta_X(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}$. The identity is etale directly from the affine definition: its ring maps are identities.

lean.statement: theorem etaleChart_localDimension {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (x : Point X.obj.obj) : (∃ (W : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a ∧ ∃ w : W.left, schemePointMap a w = x) ∧ (∀ (W₁ W₂ : Over S) (a₁ : yoneda.obj W₁ ⟶ X.obj.obj) (a₂ : yoneda.obj W₂ ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a₁ → IsEtale a₂ → ∀ (w₁ : W₁.left) (w₂ : W₂.left), schemePointMap a₁ w₁ = x → schemePointMap a₂ w₂ = x → ringKrullDim (W₁.left.presheaf.stalk w₁) = ringKrullDim (W₂.left.presheaf.stalk w₂)) ∧ ∃! d : ℕ∞, (∀ (W : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → ∀ w : W.left, schemePointMap a w = x → ringKrullDim (W.left.presheaf.stalk w) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (e : yoneda.obj T ≅ X.obj.obj) (t : T.left), schemePointMap e.hom t = x → (d : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (T.left.presheaf.stalk t))
